title: The Smallest Odd Abundant Number Coprime to 3
content: A natural number $n$ is **abundant** when $\sigma(n) > 2n$. The smallest abundant number is $12$ and the smallest *odd* one is $945 = 3^3\cdot 5\cdot 7$. Forbidding the prime $3$ makes the least example jump to the eight-prime number $5391411025 = 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23\cdot 29$, whose abundancy index $\sigma(n)/n \approx 2.00306$ barely clears $2$. This file is the **capstone** assembling the two companion halves — the witness is in the family, and nothing smaller is — into a single `IsLeast` statement.

title: The Family and the Minimality Lower Bound
content: `OddThreeFreeAbundant = {n | Odd n ∧ ¬(3∣n) ∧ Nat.Abundant n}` is the family the open question is about. `witness_mem_lowerBounds` shows $5391411025 \in \mathrm{lowerBounds}$ of this family — i.e. every odd abundant $n$ coprime to $3$ satisfies $n \ge 5391411025$ — by repackaging the hard companion theorem `odd_abundant_coprime_three_ge_witness` (assembled from the squarefree, $\omega\ge 8$, and residual $\omega = 7$ cases via a sharp rational Euler abundancy product).

title: Exact Minimality: IsLeast S 5391411025
content: `isLeast_oddThreeFreeAbundant : IsLeast OddThreeFreeAbundant 5391411025` is the headline result. Since `IsLeast S a ↔ a ∈ S ∧ a ∈ lowerBounds S`, it pairs the membership certificate (the witness is odd, coprime to $3$, and abundant — abundance via multiplicativity of $\sigma$, **no** `native_decide`) with the lower bound above. `smallest_odd_abundant_coprime_three` restates it as an explicit two-sided claim. The whole dependency chain is axiom-free: `#print axioms` shows only `propext`/`Classical.choice`/`Quot.sound`.
